title: Gulf of Alaska — 59.5°N

gallery.blurb: Radar sees a ship here. The transponder record does not. Which one is lying?

notes: Radar-versus-transponder cross-check on real data. Target acts: detect, trace, attribute, verify. Export box -142.7844 59.5021 -142.6432 59.6089, 100% inside the scene footprint, dB clamp [-29, -14]. Exported raster is 1573 x 1190 at 10 m. cerulean_slick.geojson is Cerulean slick 3630124 (2.48 km, 0.27 km2, model confidence 0.761). HONESTY FLAG, must be said before a judge says it: Cerulean's human reviewer classed this slick AMBIGUOUS — 'not clear after human review if the detection is oil or some other slick'. Our claim here is the radar-versus-AIS cross-check, not certainty that this is oil. If Stage 1 also hedges, that is a result, not a failure. HIGHEST LATITUDE IN THE LIBRARY at 59.5N: a degree of longitude here is about half as wide as at 30N, so cos(lat) errors that were invisible on the Atlantic cases will show up first here — check the exported pixel aspect ratio.
